language_task: Put the spoon in the drawer.
outcome_evidence: The first pickup loses the spoon, leaving it on the table while the empty gripper travels toward the drawer (frames 85–140, wrist_image and left_ego_image). A second pickup retains the spoon during transport (frames 270–330, wrist_image and image). The gripper releases it into the open drawer at frames 331–338; image shows the spoon remaining in the drawer as the empty gripper withdraws through frame 364. No unrelated-object disturbance or damage is visible.

failure_annotations.explanation: The spoon handle slides out of the lifting gripper at frames 85–89 in wrist_image, and the spoon settles back onto the table in left_ego_image. The robot continues toward the drawer empty and opens its fingers there around frames 137–143, while image and left_ego_image show the spoon still on the table. This failed retention and empty transfer do not advance placement; return motion begins at frame 148.
failure_annotations.recovery: Return to the spoon, align the fingers securely around its handle, and verify retention with a short lift before transporting it to the drawer; no human intervention is needed.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The spoon falls back onto the tabletop without visible damage or disturbance of other objects; the consequence is a failed transfer and wasted motion.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The spoon remains accessible on the table and the drawer remains open, so another grasp can be attempted without environmental resetting or human intervention.
